A '''linear map''', also known as a '''linear transformation''', is a [[function]] that maps one [[vector space]] to another, preserving addition and scalar multiplication.

== Formal definition ==

Let $V$ and $W$ be [[vector space]]s over the same [[field (mathematical concept)|field]] $\mathbb{F}$.

$$
T:V\to W
$$

is a '''linear map''' of $V$ to $W$ if

$$
T(\alpha \vec u+\beta \vec v)=\alpha T(\vec u)+\beta T(\vec v)
\qquad
\forall \vec u,\vec v\in V,\forall \alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{F}.
$$

When $W=V$, $T$ is called a '''linear operator''' of $V$.
